editorial.marketOverview: Nasdaq and semiconductor equities remain under substantial selling pressure. Reuters midday coverage put Nasdaq down around 3.3%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 8.6%, and Nvidia down about 7%. These direct sector observations strengthen the evidence that chip weakness is a central driver of the risk-off tape, though quotes are intraday and not tick-synchronized.
editorial.whatChanged: The main incremental improvement in evidence is Reuters' direct SOX index observation, whereas the prior report relied primarily on SMH as a semiconductor proxy. Its roughly 8.6% decline confirms sector-wide damage, but this is confirmation of the already-established 12:10 ET downside acceleration, not a separate new three-day path. Open Watch remains 174 curated events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Semiconductor underperformance, AI-valuation anxiety and elevated volatility point to deleveraging rather than a normal rotation alone. The previously reported 10Y/2Y yields imply a positive 29-basis-point curve; they are stale and cannot establish contemporaneous rates causality. Fed hike odds quoted in secondary reporting are not treated as directly verified CME pricing. Softer Michigan inflation expectations are a counterweight, not evidence of a reversal.
editorial.threeDayPath: Friday's close is decisive: persistent weakness into the auction would favor Monday downside continuation or a failed rebound. Monday and Tuesday retain bearish skew with high two-way volatility and the possibility of sharp oversold rallies. The central scenario remains unchanged from the previous published assessment; no deterministic price target is justified.
editorial.bullCase: An exhaustion rally becomes credible if QQQ and SOX recover together, volatility contracts and broad participation improves. Falling Treasury yields and improved inflation expectations can support duration-sensitive assets, but so far have not offset the technology liquidation.
editorial.bearCase: If SOX remains markedly weaker than Nasdaq and VIX stays near 30, further forced selling and weak Monday follow-through are plausible. AI financing concerns, regulatory uncertainty and tighter Fed expectations remain risk narratives, but their specific causal contribution is not independently established by synchronized market data.
